provision_review.why: 3101(b)(1) taxes the income of every individual on wages received by him, so the tax belongs to each person. The pre-fix rule computed it at TaxUnit entity on a pooled wage base. A reader can see the provision calls for Person scope, which is what the post-fix rule uses.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The 1.45 percent hospital insurance tax was carried on a TaxUnit entity although 26 USC 3101(b)(1) imposes it 'on the income of every individual' on wages 'received by him', so the encoding applied a per-individual tax to a pooled household wage base.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 0. Corpus text confirms '(b) Hospital insurance (1) In general ... imposed on the income of every individual a tax equal to 1.45 percent of the wages ... received by him with respect to employment'. Decisive change entity: TaxUnit -> Person. Other hunks are summary rewrite, span->excerpt key rename, added self-import atom for the rate, and a block-scalar reformat of the 0.0145 literal (value unchanged). Note the added atom for the 'wages ... received by him with respect to employment' excerpt is typed kind: condition here while the parallel atom in 3101(a) is typed kind: definition - inconsistent atom typing, not a fidelity issue. Message/PR generic, so confidence held below 0.8.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as provenance-only churn and could not: apart from span -> excerpt, a summary paraphrase, block-scalar reformatting of 0.0145, and two added proof atoms, the one substantive line flips hospital_insurance_wage_tax from entity: TaxUnit to entity: Person, which is the rule's declared population and output surface. The pinned corpus text for us/statute/26/3101 reads "there is hereby imposed on the income of every individual a tax equal to 1.45 percent of the wages (as defined in section 3121(a)) received by him with respect to employment", so the individual, not the tax unit, is the source-supported entity. The formula (wages * hospital_insurance_wage_tax_rate), the 0.0145 rate, the 1986-01-01 effective date and the companion test expectations are all unchanged, so entity is the only meaning that moved and wrong_entity_or_scope fits.
triage.verifier_notes: Evidence quality: the first reader's quote ("refresh generated RuleSpec artifacts for the Chapter 21 FICA wage/tax chain...") is generic PR-body text and does not itself evidence the entity fix; the decisive evidence is the diff line above plus the pinned provision text, so the corpus record should carry that quote instead. Scope correction to the reader's record: only `hospital_insurance_wage_tax` changed entity; `hospital_insurance_wage_tax_rate` is `kind: parameter` and its only changes were `span:` -> `excerpt:` and `formula: '0.0145'` -> a block scalar (mechanical), so listing it in rule_names overstates the fix. Residual doubt worth flagging: 3101(b)(1) is an uncapped linear 1.45% tax, so a TaxUnit-level encoding could produce the same aggregate dollar total as the sum of per-person taxes; the defect is the population/output surface (and everything downstream that needs a per-individual Medicare figure, e.g. the (b)(2) additional tax thresholds), not a changed household total. I did not read the engine's entity-aggregation semantics, so I do not endorse the reader's specific mechanism claim that the pre-fix rule "applied a per-individual tax to a pooled household wage base" — the module's own input is `us:statutes/26/3101/b/1#input.wages`, whose level follows the rule entity; the scope defect holds without that claim. Companion tests (statutes/26/3101/b/1.test.yaml) changed only in case names and are entity-agnostic single-scalar cases, so they neither confirm nor refute; sibling module statutes/26/3101/a.yaml took the same TaxUnit->Person correction in this commit.
